headline: Chip Rout Caps a Brutal Week as Gulf Tensions Cloud the Road Ahead
body_html:
Wall Street ended Friday's session, November 20, on its heels. Of the 662 stocks in our universe, 554 fell and only 102 rose. The slide capped a week that one major outlet called the market's worst in over a year, with the S&P 500 now spoken of as being in correction territory.

Semiconductors took the heaviest blow, with the sector down 10.02%. Applied Optoelectronics fell 16.55%, Sandisk 16.05%, Celestica 16.0%, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 15.32%, Bloom Energy 15.3% and Credo Technology 15.2%. The damage spread well beyond chips. Financials lost 3.53%, energy 3.32%, materials 3.16% and industrials 3.14%. Homebuilders were the only group to finish higher, up 0.32%.

Monday, November 23, brings the first test of whether selling has run its course. Traders will also watch the Gulf. Iran says it wants diplomacy to end the conflict, yet Washington calls the terms unacceptable, and a Qatari delegation is in Tehran. Reports of tanker incidents near Hormuz add to the risk, so oil and shipping headlines may drive sentiment as much as earnings do.

briefs.headline: Chip complex suffers a double-digit sector drop
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 10.02% on Friday, the worst showing of any group we track. Memory, power-chip and connectivity names were all hit with losses of 15% or more. Monday will show whether buyers return or the pressure carries into the new week.

briefs.headline: Apparel retailers buck the selling
briefs.body: Gap rose 11.44% and Buckle gained 5.67%, two of the session's strongest performers. Spectrum Brands added 6.3%. Even so, the consumer sector as a whole slipped 1.37%, so the strength looked like a handful of stock-specific stories rather than a broad shift.

briefs.headline: Iran talks send mixed signals
briefs.body: Tehran's foreign minister says Iran wants diplomacy to end the war, but President Trump says the terms on offer are unacceptable. A Qatari delegation visiting Tehran gives mediation some momentum. Markets will react to any sign the two sides are moving closer.

briefs.headline: Shipping risks build near Hormuz
briefs.body: Britain's maritime agency reported two tanker incidents near Oman, and Iran said a vessel struck a mine east of Hormuz. Bahrain and Saudi Arabia also reported intercepting attacks. Energy stocks fell 3.32% Friday despite the tension, so oil-linked names deserve close watching.

briefs.headline: Washington tightens the screws on Iranian oil money
briefs.body: The Treasury has sanctioned Iranian intermediaries accused of collecting oil revenue on Tehran's behalf. The move signals continued economic pressure even as diplomatic channels stay open. Investors will watch for any effect on crude flows in the coming days.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders hold on to a thin gain
briefs.body: Homebuilders rose 0.32% and were the only group in positive territory on a day when 554 stocks fell. Software lost 2.1% and healthcare 1.63%, though Heartflow and Klaviyo posted gains of 4.62% and 4.41%. Defensive pockets were hard to find, but a few existed.
